newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SGB says Electrabel merger could be years away.
newsitem.headline: SGB says Electrabel merger could be years away.

text.p: Belgian holding company Societe Generale de Belgique (SGB) said on Thursday that a merger of its utility units Tractebel and Electrabel could be some way off.
"It is not sure a merger will happen, definitely not soon. It could be years away," an SGB spokesman said.

On Wednesday, Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene's office said the government favoured a Tractebel-Electrabel merger in order to protect Belgian interests from French dominance. Electrabel has a virtual monopoly on electricity production in Belgium.

Tractebel, which owns 39.4 percent of Electrabel, is 50.3 percent owned by SGB, itself 62.61 percent owned by French Compagnie de Suez, which is set to merge with French utility group Lyonnaise des Eaux.
SGB, in a joint statement with Suez late on Wednesday, said it had no objections in principle to a merger, provided it could keep majority control of the merged Tractebel-Electrabel unit.
Earlier on Wednesday, the group had said it would be willing to be diluted below 50 percent in the merged unit.

The SGB spokesman said that as Electrabel's stock market capitalisation of 440 billion francs is double that of Tractebel's 220 billion, a merger of the two would dilute SGB's stake in the new unit to 25 percent.
He said it would cost SGB 120 billion francs to keep its stake in a merger Tractebel-Electrabel above 50 percent. "But that is a theoretical figure," he added.
Analysts say that SGB -- which already has debts of about 20 billion francs -- would have to liquidate three quarters of its portfolio in order to raise that amount.

SGB is Belgium's largest and oldest holding company. Besides Tractebel, it controls Generale Bank and Fortis AG, the country's biggest bank and biggest insurance company, along with assets in the steel, chemical and non-ferrous metals sector.
The new Suez-Lyonnaise group -- which focusses on utility services -- has said that with the exception of Tractebel, all SGB's assets are considered non-core.
